title: Telemetry catchup orchestration adapter for resumable analytics replays
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem statement:

We occasionally receive late or mutated telemetry (usage events, job traces) that must be reprocessed into downstream analytics and billing pipelines. Existing replay tooling is brittle for long-running, large-volume catchups: jobs time out, duplicate rows slip through, and manual intervention is required for shard rebalancing. This ticket creates a lightweight orchestration adapter that coordinates resumable catchup runs across shards with strong idempotency, backpressure controls, and cost-awareness.

Goals / scope:
- Provide an orchestration layer that can spawn and track resumable worker segments (shards) for a single backfill/replay job.
- Ensure end-to-end idempotency and at-least-once guarantees without duplicate metrics in BigQuery/Postgres destinations.
- Support pause/resume with resume tokens per shard and global checkpointing.
- Implement cost-safeguards (max tokens/sec per job, slot-based budget enforcement) and automatic throttling.
- Emit rich observability (per-shard progress, reprocess lag, estimated remaining cost) into Console and existing telemetry dashboards.
- Integrate with existing replayer runners and the reprocess orchestration API surface used by Console backend services.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting existing worker serialization formats. Adapter will translate between existing worker contracts and the orchestration state.

Design summary:
1) Job model: a Job record contains job_id, source_range (time or seq window), manifest of logical shards, target destination table, budget bounds, and checkpoint interval. Jobs are created by Console or automated monitors when drift is detected.

2) Shard runners: lightweight idempotent workers own a shard token and process incrementally. Each shard writes progress checkpoints to the orchestration datastore (durable, strongly consistent store). Checkpoints include last_processed_seq, checkpoint_hash, and a resume_token.

3) Coordinator/Adapter: a stateless adapter service accepts job requests and performs orchestration decisions: allocate shards to runner pool, rebalance stuck shards, pause/resume jobs, enforce budget windows. The adapter uses a leader lease to avoid split-brain when multiple replicas are deployed.

4) Safety & idempotency: workers must perform idempotent writes to downstream by using deterministic dedupe keys and a lightweight per-destination sequential watermark. The adapter will surface the canonical commit watermark per-job to simplify idempotency for ad-hoc sinks.

5) Observability: expose a Console route for job details and per-shard timelines, integrate with existing tracing and metrics (span: reprocess.shard.process, metric: reprocess.records_processed, log: reprocess.checkpoint).*

6) Failure modes & retries: exponential backoff + jitter for transient failures; dead-lettering of unprocessable batches with a retry window and paginated inspection in the Console UI.

Success criteria:
- A 10M-event historical catchup job can complete without manual shard reassignment in a single run for 95% of cases.
- Duplicate rows in target sinks < 1 per 1M events measured in canary runs.
- Operator can pause and resume any job with < 30s to pick up using resume tokens.
- Cost controls prevent jobs from exceeding configured monthly budget in 100% of test runs.

Acceptance Criteria (tests to verify):
acceptance_criteria: Create job manifest API and persist a simple job with 50 shards
Start job and see per-shard checkpoints written every 30s in orchestration datastore
Pause job mid-run and resume; verify last_processed_seq is honored and no duplicates are emitted
Introduce transient worker failure and verify adapter reassigns shard after lease expiry
Run synthetic 1M-event canary and verify duplicates < 1 per 1M events
Expose metrics in Console: reprocess.progress, reprocess.eta_ms, reprocess.cost_estimate

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Long-running jobs may exhaust ephemeral worker pools -> Mitigation: slot-based accounting and preemptible worker lanes
Risk: Out-of-order late events break dedupe logic -> Mitigation: per-shard reordering window and watermark based commits
Risk: Large number of tiny shards creates overhead -> Mitigation: shard bucketing and adaptive coalescing during job creation
Risk: Cost overruns from runaway reprocess -> Mitigation: global budget caps and automatic pause when budget > threshold
rollout_plan: Alpha run: internal-only on staging with synthetic datasets (1 week)
Beta: opt-in customers and internal ops teams with small dataset (2 weeks)
Full rollout: enable for jobs created via Console and automated monitors with alerting hooks enabled
qa_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint serialization and resume token handling
Integration tests with worker harness and a Postgres/BigQuery sink emulator
Load test: 10 concurrent jobs each with 100k events; measure wall time and duplicate rate
Chaos test: kill adapter replica and ensure lease failover doesn't create duplicate work
